**Notes and Explanations:**
I focused the CV on supported React/TypeScript work, accessibility, testing, and the Node.js/Express/PostgreSQL experience demonstrated in the Tidewatch project. I included the teaching assistant role, hackathon result, and relevant portfolio projects. I did not claim 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience, end-to-end testing, web security expertise, or healthcare experience because the supplied material does not establish these. The candidate is based in Dublin, while the advertised remote locations are Austria, Germany, Croatia, or Slovenia; the CV does not imply eligibility to work remotely from one of those countries. Per instruction, I have provided a CV only, not a cover letter.

Please review the CV and let me know if you'd like any modifications.

**CV Quality Assessment:**
Quality Score: 78/100

**Content Quality:**
This is a clear, well-structured junior developer CV with strong evidence of React, TypeScript, accessibility, Node.js, PostgreSQL, testing, Next.js and Storybook work. The Tidewatch project is particularly relevant and well quantified through its Lighthouse score, technologies, testing tools and project grade. The teaching-assistant experience also supports the role's mentoring expectations. The main content limitation is that the CV presents several academic and project-based capabilities alongside limited professional experience, while the target role requests a more experienced full-stack engineer. Some claims are broad: automated testing is stated, but only unit testing is evidenced; backend experience is present mainly through a final-year project rather than employment. No unsupported skills or experiences were detected when cross-referenced with the supplied candidate information.

**ATS Compatibility:**
The CV is ATS-friendly overall: it uses conventional headings, simple text structure, chronological experience, explicit technology names and no apparent tables, graphics or multi-column formatting. Keyword coverage is strong for React, TypeScript, Node.js, Express, PostgreSQL, accessibility, Jest, Git/GitHub, Next.js and Storybook. AI screening probability for this specific vacancy is moderate to low because several must-have terms are either absent or only partially evidenced: 2+ years of professional React/TypeScript experience, semantic HTML, responsive layouts, end-to-end testing, web security fundamentals/OWASP Top 10, and health-data privacy. The plain-text links should ideally be written as complete URLs, such as https://github.com/... and https://... , to improve parsing and usability.

**Job Alignment:**
The strongest alignment is with the patient-facing and accessibility aspects of the role. The candidate has built a wellness booking site, an accessible public-information application, React/TypeScript interfaces, a Node.js/Express API, PostgreSQL storage, Storybook documentation and accessible components tested with NVDA and VoiceOver. The candidate also demonstrates English fluency and some mentoring experience through teaching approximately 30 students. However, the candidate's material does not demonstrate two or more years of professional React/TypeScript experience, end-to-end testing, OWASP/security awareness, or health-data privacy work. AWS/Docker, German/Croatian, analytics/A/B testing and NestJS are also not evidenced. These are candidate-profile gaps rather than CV-writing defects. The remote preference and location may also be a practical issue: the candidate is in Dublin, while the advertised remote locations are Austria, Germany, Croatia or Slovenia; the CV should not imply eligibility for this arrangement.

**What your material does not show for this job (left out, not faked):**
- 2+ years of professional experience building web applications with React and TypeScript
- Understanding of semantic HTML, responsive layouts and web accessibility basics
- Experience with automated testing (unit and end-to-end) and Git-based workflows
- Awareness of web security fundamentals (authentication, OWASP Top 10)
- Willingness to learn the privacy requirements of health data
- German or Croatian for customer-facing conversations
- Familiarity with AWS or a similar cloud, and with Docker
- Experience with analytics and A/B testing

**Improvement Suggestions:**
CRITICAL / HIGH-VALUE CHANGES
1. In the Professional Summary, make the distinction between professional experience and project experience explicit so the CV does not appear to overstate seniority. Replace the sentence beginning "Junior frontend developer with hands-on experience" with wording such as: "Junior frontend developer with professional internship and freelance experience, plus substantial academic project experience building React and TypeScript web applications. Built an accessible sea-swimming app with a Node.js/Express API and PostgreSQL database, and improved accessibility, testing and Storybook documentation during a software development internship." 
2. In the Professional Summary and the Tidewatch project, describe testing precisely as unit testing rather than implying broader test coverage. For example, change "Experienced with accessibility improvements, automated testing" to "Experienced with accessibility improvements and automated unit testing using Jest and React Testing Library." Do not add end-to-end testing because it is not present in the candidate information.
3. In the Study Buddy project bullet, add the supported authentication detail so the CV shows the closest available evidence for the security/authentication portion of the job: change the bullet to "Built the React frontend and login screens for a study-session matching web app in a four-person student team; used Firebase Authentication for user sign-in, while other team members developed the API and database." Do not describe this as OWASP or web-security experience, because that is not supported.
4. In the Technical Skills section, make the testing and accessibility scope more exact. Change "Testing and tools: Jest, React Testing Library, Git/GitHub, Storybook, Figma" to "Testing: Jest, React Testing Library (unit testing) | Tools and collaboration: Git/GitHub, Storybook, Figma." This improves accuracy and prevents an ATS or recruiter from assuming that Playwright or end-to-end testing is available.
5. In the header, convert both links into complete, clickable URLs, for example "GitHub: https://github.com/aiyana-bt-example | Portfolio: https://aiyana-bt.example.com". Retain the simple one-line contact format and avoid icons or graphics.

MINOR / OPTIONAL ENHANCEMENTS
6. In the Freelance experience entry, make the wellness relevance more explicit without overstating it. Change "Built a booking website for a local yoga studio" to "Built a wellness booking website for a local yoga studio using Next.js and Tailwind CSS, including class timetables and email-based booking requests." 
7. In the Tidewatch project, retain the exact accessibility evidence but make the standards and testing terms more scannable by changing the final testing bullet to: "Tested with NVDA and VoiceOver; achieved a Lighthouse accessibility score of 100." The current content is already truthful; this is only a clarity adjustment.
8. In the Experience section, keep the Teaching Assistant role because it is supported by the candidate information and relevant to the advert's mentoring requirement. Its bullet could be made more specific without inventing duties: "Supported approximately 30 first-year students during one semester of web development labs." The current wording is already acceptable, so this is a minor refinement only.

The candidate also lacks evidence of end-to-end testing, web security fundamentals, GDPR or health-data privacy, AWS/Docker, German/Croatian, analytics/A-B testing, and regulated healthcare experience. job_description_info.job_description:
# Full-Stack Engineer (TypeScript / React) – Patient Experience

**Company:** Verdane Care (FICTIONAL)
**Location:** Graz, Austria (hybrid) or fully remote within Austria, Germany, Croatia or Slovenia
**Employment:** Full-time, permanent (or B2B contract in Croatia on request)
**Team:** Patient Experience squad (4 engineers, 1 designer, 1 product manager)

## About the role

Verdane Care makes appointment-booking and follow-up software for private clinics and physiotherapy practices. Patients use our web app and mobile web experience to book visits, fill in intake forms, receive reminders and view exercise plans.

As a Full-Stack Engineer you will build and improve those patient-facing features end to end – from React components and accessibility to the Node.js APIs and the database behind them. You will work in a small squad with a designer and a product manager, and you will ship to production several times a week.

## What you will do

- Build new patient-facing features in React and TypeScript, with a strong focus on accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA) and performance on low-end phones
- Implement Node.js (NestJS) APIs and PostgreSQL schemas to support those features
- Integrate with third-party systems such as clinic calendars, SMS providers and payment gateways
- Write unit, integration and end-to-end tests (Jest, Playwright) and keep the build green
- Take part in design reviews, usability sessions and sprint planning
- Handle personal health data responsibly: follow our GDPR and data-minimisation guidelines, support audit requests from clinic customers
- Mentor interns or junior colleagues when the opportunity arises

## What you bring

**Must have**
- 2+ years of professional experience building web applications with React and TypeScript
- Experience writing backend services in Node.js (Express, NestJS or similar) and working with SQL databases
- Understanding of semantic HTML, responsive layouts and web accessibility basics
- Experience with automated testing (unit and end-to-end) and Git-based workflows
- Awareness of web security fundamentals (authentication, OWASP Top 10) and willingness to learn the privacy requirements of health data
- Fluent English; German or Croatian is helpful for customer-facing conversations

**Nice to have**
- Experience with Next.js or other server-side rendering frameworks
- Experience in healthcare, wellness or other regulated environments
- Familiarity with AWS or a similar cloud, and with Docker
- Experience with design systems and Storybook
- Experience with analytics and A/B testing

## What we offer

- Salary range EUR 54,000 – 70,000 gross per year depending on experience (Austrian collective agreement minimum applies)
- 25 days of holiday plus the Austrian public holidays, 5 additional well-being days and a EUR 1,200 yearly education budget
- Flexible hours, a home-office stipend and a yearly team retreat
- A friendly, low-ego team that cares about the people who use our software

## How to apply

Send your CV. A short cover letter and a link to something you have built (a portfolio, a GitHub project or a live site) are welcome but optional. We reply within ten working days.

Verdane Care is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace and welcomes applications from career changers and people returning to work.

Verdane Care is a healthcare technology company founded in Graz in 2019. It develops software that helps private clinics, physiotherapy practices and dental offices manage appointments and patient communication. Its products include online booking and reminders, secure digital intake and consent forms, and exercise plans and follow-up messages for physiotherapy patients. More than 1,900 practices across Austria, Germany, Croatia and Slovenia use its services.

The company’s stated principles are **“Patients first,” “Privacy by default,” and “Simple beats clever.”** It prioritises secure handling of patient data, with ISO 27001 certification and EU-based data hosting, and builds its applications to WCAG 2.2 AA accessibility standards. Verdane describes its goal as making healthcare feel more human and care simpler for patients and clinics.

Verdane has 68 employees across Graz and Ljubljana, with some remote colleagues, and is expanding its engineering team. Its listed engineering practices include optional pair programming and weekly demonstrations with clinic staff—suggesting a collaborative, user-focused working environment where teams can learn directly from the people who use their software.

# Verdane Care in the news
*(fictional news item – verdanecare.example/blog/new-patient-app)*

## Verdane Care launches redesigned patient app and opens engineering hub in Ljubljana
**Graz, 22 September 2026**

Verdane Care, the Graz-based provider of appointment-booking software for private clinics, has launched a completely redesigned patient experience built on a new React-based design system. The new app cuts the median booking time from 94 to 41 seconds and passes the WCAG 2.2 AA audit commissioned from an independent accessibility consultancy.

The company also opened a small engineering hub in Ljubljana, Croatia, to recruit developers who prefer working in the Adriatic time zone. "Great engineers do not all live in Graz," said co-founder and CTO Jure Kovač. "We are hiring full-stack engineers who care about accessibility and about the people who will use the software."

Co-founder and CEO Dr. Lena Moser announced that Verdane will release a public developer API for clinic software vendors in spring 2027. The company says all patient data remains in EU data centres and that Verdane was recently re-certified under ISO 27001 without findings.

Verdane employs 68 people and plans to hire eight engineers, two designers and one data protection specialist before mid-2027.
# Careers at Verdane Care
*(fictional careers page – verdanecare.example/careers)*

## Join us and make healthcare feel human

**Engineering at Verdane**
- Front end: React, TypeScript, Next.js (marketing and clinic web), Storybook design system, Playwright
- Back end: Node.js (NestJS), PostgreSQL, Redis; AWS (Frankfurt region), Docker, GitHub Actions
- Practices: pair programming on request, weekly demos with real clinic staff, accessibility checks in CI, quarterly security reviews
- We are a small team: every engineer has a visible impact on the product within the first month.

**Benefits:** flexible hours, home-office stipend, EUR 1,200 education budget, 5 well-being days, annual retreat, mental-health support through an external provider.

**Hiring process:** short screening call (30 min) -> technical conversation (60 min, we look at a project you built) -> pairing session on a small realistic task (90 min) -> meeting with the founders.

**What we value:** curiosity, care for users, honesty about what you do not know. Career changers and bootcamp graduates with real projects are welcome to apply.

**Open roles:** Full-Stack Engineer (TypeScript/React) – Patient Experience · QA Engineer · Data Protection Specialist · Customer Support Lead (DACH)
